why: The fix in a622768 replaces the throwing indexer `DiscountRates[order.DiscountCode]` with `TryGetValue`, so an unknown or retired code such as SUMMER25 returns the subtotal, as the runbook expects. It fixes the cause the investigator named, not the symptom. Valid codes are unchanged: the rate lookup and `Math.Round(subtotal * (1 - rate), 2)` are the same as before, and the existing test GetOrderTotal_AppliesTheDiscountCode (order 1001, WELCOME10, 26.10) still covers that path. Null or empty codes still return the subtotal via the existing IsNullOrEmpty guard, and GetOrderTotal_WithoutDiscount_IsTheSubtotal covers that case. The new regression test in Regression/OrderTotalRetiredCodeTests.cs checks order 1003 (SUMMER25, expected 35.00) and order 1004 (VIP20, expected 63.92), and its doc comment matches the behaviour. Order lookup still goes through _orders.Get, so OrderNotFoundException for unknown ids is untouched. Not part of this fix, for the record: DiscountLabel.cs parses the rate from the last two characters of the code, so it has its own assumption about code format. It does not throw KeyNotFoundException and is outside this case, so it is not a reason to send the fix back.
